summary.note: Reentrancy cluster (5 raw items) collapsed to one mitigated/not-exploitable note. Two loop/info items map to existing open ledger entries (left for sanitizer reconciliation). SA-007 dropped as tool noise. Two NEW econ findings preserved with severity hints.

findings.title: Sequential migrateOut batch exits through AMM-backed strategy distribute non-uniform haircuts across identical-principal users
findings.rootCause: Per-batch haircut ratio computed as payout/totalPrincipal using only the current batch's principal against a single aggregate strategy exit; sequential batch exits walk the AMM price down so earlier batches realize smaller haircuts than later batches.
findings.impactSummary: Cross-user value-leak / unfairness: two users with identical principal in different batches receive materially different haircuts even under honest migrator ordering. Conservation holds (no theft, no protocol loss).
preconditions: Strategy is fee/slippage-bearing (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy selling vault shares through an AMM)
findings.dedupNotes: Distinct from ledger M-01 (requested-vs-received mismatch, acknowledged/fixed by this diff) and from wont-fix 'underwater buffer FCFS-at-par' Medium: different root cause (intra-batch AMM price walk vs at-par FCFS ordering). Sanitizer to confirm no overlap with wont-fix FCFS entry.

findings.title: Haircut scaling branch keyed on payout<totalPrincipal rather than _isUnderwater
findings.rootCause: Scaling path is entered on `payout < totalPrincipal` (true under benign ERC4626 redeem rounding favoring the vault) instead of an explicit `_isUnderwater` check, so healthy/at-par pools apply a sub-wei dust haircut.
findings.impactSummary: Negligible value (sub-wei dust); spec-accuracy / state-handling note.

findings.title: Unbounded per-batch external-call loop in migrateOut
findings.rootCause: users[] / migrator loop in migrateOut performs external calls per iteration; bound is operator-controlled and getStakersRange pagination exists.
findings.impactSummary: Operator-controlled DoS surface; mitigated by privileged batch caller and pagination.
findings.dedupNotes: SA-005 (Slither calls-in-loop) and PATTERN-002 (DOS-UNBOUNDED-LOOP) are the same root cause. Maps to existing OPEN ledger entry 'unbounded per-user external-call loop in migrateOut (Low)'. Forwarded to sanitizer; do not re-report as new.
